agree.reason: The memo is clear about the risk, sets checkpoints the board can hold the director to, and offers resuming ads as a fallback, which should win most of the board; the two members from ad sales may still want to see what membership will cost to run, and the memo doesn't say.

honest.reason: Every figure is either taken from the brief or worked out correctly from it, and the memo turns the brief's "replace within a year" into a carefully worded run-rate target with a 2027 cash estimate; its one stretch is calling the $131k-to-$84k fall "twelve months" when the brief only says "two years ago".

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the pilot's annual value, the share of the list that joined, the 875-member target, the 55-a-month pace needed against the roughly 150 a month the pilot reached, the $34k ad projection, and the roughly $52k of membership income in the build-up year, and all of these are correct.

right_comparison.reason: It sets membership against ads on their actual downward trend ($34k projected for 2027) rather than a flat $84k, and compares the partial-year membership income with that same declining figure.

qualification.reason: It names early-adopter bias and cancellations as the risks and sets three dated member counts, but only the March checkpoint has a stated consequence (options to the board in April, including resuming ads).

objections.reason: It answers "why not run both" and handles the ad colleague with care, but it doesn't address what the membership program and its marketing will cost, or whether more selling effort could slow the ad decline, which the members from sales are likely to raise.

fit.reason: It is a proper board memo with a clear decision request and tight sections, at about one page, perhaps running slightly over.
